plan.planning_summary: The problem requires designing and optimizing all-dielectric polarizing beam splitters (PBS) on fused silica at 45 degrees incidence across 500-650 nm. The design space involves discrete material choices (MgF2, SiO2, Ta2O5, TiO2) and continuous thickness variables (25-220 nm). Three distinct layer counts (6, 10, 14) must be evaluated to balance performance against complexity. Since no literature evidence is provided, the routes are theory-based, relying on standard thin-film interference principles for PBS operation (Brewster-angle-like behavior or high-index contrast Bragg reflection for TE vs TM transmission). Each route will optimize the specific topology for its layer count. Robustness analysis (thickness error sigma=1.5%, angle error +/-1 deg) will be included in the execution request for each optimized candidate.

routes.title: Optimization of 6-Layer All-Dielectric Polarizing Beam Splitter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 6-layer stack utilizing high-index contrast materials (TiO2/SiO2 or Ta2O5/SiO2) can achieve mean TE reflectance >90% and mean TM transmittance >85% at 45 degrees incidence across 500-650 nm by leveraging destructive interference for TM polarization and constructive reflection for TE polarization within the limited degrees of freedom.
routes.design_principle: Maximize refractive index contrast between adjacent layers to enhance polarization selectivity. Use a symmetric or near-symmetric structure to manage phase accumulation. Optimize thicknesses to create a 'polarization-dependent bandgap' where TE is reflected and TM is transmitted.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica
manufacturing_considerations: High-index TiO2 may require precise stoichiometry control
Low total layer count simplifies fabrication but reduces spectral bandwidth control
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory for polarizing beam splitters
Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for planar multilayer systems
Refractive index dispersion data for TiO2 and SiO2 in visible spectrum
expected_advantages: Simplest structure with lowest material cost and deposition time
Potentially highest robustness due to fewer interfaces and thinner total stack
known_risks: Limited degrees of freedom may prevent simultaneous satisfaction of both TE R and TM T targets across the full 150 nm bandwidth
Sensitivity to thickness errors may be higher due to narrower operational bandwidth
routes.execution_request_english: Perform a numerical optimization of a 6-layer all-dielectric polarizing beam splitter on a fused silica substrate. Incident medium: Air. Substrate: Fused Silica. Incidence angle: 45 degrees. Wavelength range: 500-650 nm. Materials: TiO2 and SiO2 for the coating layers. Stack sequence: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica. Design variables: Thicknesses of all 6 coating layers, bounded between 25 nm and 220 nm. Objective: Maximize a composite score that rewards Mean TE Reflectance (target >= 90%) and Mean TM Transmittance (target >= 85%), while penalizing total physical thickness. After finding the optimal thicknesses, perform a robustness analysis by simulating the response with independent normally distributed layer-thickness errors (sigma = 1.5% of nominal thickness) and a common incidence-angle offset uniformly distributed between -1 and +1 degree. Report the optimal thicknesses, the mean TE reflectance, mean TM transmittance, total thickness, and the statistical distribution of performance under uncertainty. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 45 degrees. polarization s, p. wavelength intervals 500-650 nm. soft objectives: high TE reflectance (mean >= 90%); high TM transmittance (mean >= 85%); fewer layers; lower total thickness. robustness conditions: layer thicknesses bounded between 25 nm and 220 nm; total layer counts restricted to 6, 10, or 14.

routes.title: Optimization of 10-Layer All-Dielectric Polarizing Beam Splitter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 10-layer stack provides sufficient degrees of freedom to better shape the spectral response, allowing for flatter TE reflectance and TM transmittance profiles across the 500-650 nm band compared to the 6-layer case, potentially achieving higher average performance metrics.
routes.design_principle: Utilize the additional layers to fine-tune the phase matching conditions for both polarizations. A longer stack allows for more gradual transitions in effective refractive index, which can broaden the bandwidth of the polarization splitting effect. Consider alternating high/low index pairs with varying optical thicknesses.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Fused Silica
manufacturing_considerations: Ta2O5 offers good mechanical stability and moderate refractive index
Increased layer count increases deposition time and potential for cumulative error
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory for polarizing beam splitters
Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for planar multilayer systems
Refractive index dispersion data for Ta2O5 and SiO2 in visible spectrum
expected_advantages: Better spectral flatness and higher average performance than 6-layer design
More robust to minor thickness variations due to broader operational features
known_risks: Higher total thickness and layer count increase fabrication complexity
Potential for increased absorption if high-index materials have non-negligible k-values in this band

routes.title: Optimization of 14-Layer All-Dielectric Polarizing Beam Splitter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 14-layer stack offers the highest flexibility among the considered options, enabling the design of a broadband polarizing beam splitter with superior performance metrics (higher TE R, higher TM T) and potentially wider bandwidth, albeit at the cost of increased complexity and thickness.
routes.design_principle: Use the extended number of layers to approximate an ideal anti-reflection coating for TM polarization and a high-reflectivity mirror for TE polarization simultaneously. This may involve chirped layer thicknesses or complex multi-cavity structures to flatten the spectral response.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica
manufacturing_considerations: Highest fabrication complexity among the three options
Longest deposition time and highest risk of cumulative thickness errors
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory for polarizing beam splitters
Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for planar multilayer systems
Refractive index dispersion data for TiO2 and SiO2 in visible spectrum
expected_advantages: Best possible performance metrics (highest TE R, TM T) due to maximum degrees of freedom
Widest operational bandwidth and flattest spectral response
known_risks: Most sensitive to manufacturing tolerances due to high complexity
Diminishing returns on performance improvement relative to added cost and complexity
Total thickness may approach limits of stress management in thin films

research_influence: No literature evidence was available; thus, all routes are derived from first-principles thin-film optics theory.

The choice of TiO2/SiO2 for 6 and 14 layers and Ta2O5/SiO2 for 10 layers reflects a strategy to test different high-index materials to see if one offers better dispersion properties for the specific 45-degree incidence condition.

The explicit separation into 6, 10, and 14 layer routes ensures that the trade-off between performance and complexity is evaluated independently for each fixed topology, as required by the problem statement.
unresolved_decisions: Whether TiO2 or Ta2O5 provides superior performance for this specific application is unknown and will be determined by the optimization results.
The exact weighting of the composite objective function (performance vs. complexity) is subjective; the solver should use a reasonable default or report Pareto fronts if possible.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
